intro: Engineered roller conveyor chain has heavy sidebars, hardened pins and bushings, and rollers that carry the load along the conveyor track. It runs in bulk-handling, unit-handling, lumber, cement and processing plants, in pitches from about 1.5 to 18 inches.

Metric conveyor chain is built to DIN 8167/8165, ISO 1977 and BS 4116, sized by breaking load and pitch in millimetres. Each series comes with small, flanged or large rollers, or as bush chain, and with solid or hollow pins.
Precision roller chain to ANSI B29.1 and ISO 606 (BS), for drives and light conveying. Single and multi-strand, in standard, heavy and specialty builds.

Engineered chains made for one job — reclaimers, steel mills, glass, paper, wood, food and automotive lines. Many are built to the conveyor maker's drawing; give us the number on the sidebar and we match it.
Hollow-pin chain has a bored pin, so cross-rods, slats and fixtures bolt straight through the chain without welded attachments. Used for pallet, panel, bottle and food conveyors.
Engineering-class drive chain transmits power at low speed and high load — offset-sidebar and straight-sidebar roller chains for mills, kilns, mixers and heavy drives.
Bushed chain has no rollers: the hardened bushing runs directly on the sprocket and the chain slides on its sidebars. It suits drag, elevator and scraper duty where rollers would clog or wear out.
Agricultural roller chain (CA and A-series) for combines, balers, planters and harvesters, with the attachments these machines use.
Sharp-top chain has pointed sidebars that grip and carry boards, logs and panels through sawmill and wood-processing machines.
Round-link chain is made from welded round steel links, case-hardened for wear. It is used on bucket elevators, scraper and drag conveyors, and in mining.

Welded steel mill chain has offset sidebars and welded barrels for tough, abrasive conveying in sawmills, pulp mills and bulk handling. WR chains have heat-treated pins; WH chains have all parts heat-treated.
Accumulation chain carries products on top rollers that turn faster than the chain, or let the load stop and queue while the chain keeps running. Used on assembly and pallet lines.
Bucket elevator chain lifts bulk material in buckets — bushed, roller and round-link types for cement, grain, fertiliser and minerals.
Welded steel drag chain is built with wide, straight sidebars to drag material along a trough. Used for ash, wood waste, chips and other abrasive bulk.
Sugar mill chain for cane carriers, intermediate carriers, bagasse and diffuser conveyors — heavy welded and roller chains built for wet, abrasive, acidic service.
Double-pitch roller chain has twice the pitch of standard roller chain. It is lighter and lower in cost for long, slow conveyors, with standard or large rollers.

Drop-forged chain is built from one-piece forged links joined by pins or bolts. The links are case-hardened, so a very hard wear surface sits over a tough, shock-resistant core. It is made for drag, en-masse, scraper and case conveyors carrying grain, wood chips, ash, cement and other abrasive bulk materials. Pitches run from 102 to 260 mm (4 to 10 in) in single, double and triple strand, with welded, clamped or bolt-on (Bolt 'N' Go) flights.
Collector chain moves sludge and scum in water and wastewater clarifiers — cast, engineered steel and non-metallic chains made for submerged service.
Cast drag chain has wide cast links that drag material along the conveyor floor. Built for ash, clinker, sludge and other heavy, abrasive loads.
Combination chain joins cast block links with steel sidebars and pins. Built for elevators and conveyors in rough, abrasive service.
Pintle chain has cast or steel links joined by pins, with a closed barrel that keeps grit out of the joint. Used for drag conveyors and slow drives.
Bar-and-pin chain is simple steel bars joined by pins, with no bushings or rollers. Used for tough drag and transfer work in steel, wood and bulk plants.
Chains with clips, grippers or spikes that hold film, sheet or paper as it moves through thermoforming, printing and packaging machines.
Detachable chain has links that hook together and come apart by hand, with no tools. Used for light conveyors, drives and agricultural machines.
Chains for kilns, coolers, ovens and furnaces, in alloys and constructions that keep their strength at high temperature.
Step chain for escalators and moving walks, with rollers that carry the steps or pallets.

Drop-forged rivetless chain has three forged parts per pitch: a centre link, two side links and a T-head pin that locks in without rivets. It assembles and comes apart by hand, has open joints that shed material, and is very strong for its weight. It is widely used on flight, scraper, trolley and assembly conveyors, in sizes from X-348 to 9148, including barloop versions with flat sidebars for welding attachments.
Draw bench chain pulls bar, tube and wire through the dies of a draw bench. It is heavy chain built for very high, steady pull.
Cast chain has cast links (malleable, Promal or steel) joined by pins. Used for elevators, conveyors and drives in rough service.
Long-link chain has longer links than standard round-link chain — lighter for its length, for conveying and lifting where the long pitch suits the sprocket.
Double flex chain bends sideways as well as up and down, so one chain can run around curves on conveyors and assembly lines.
